rationale: Start with a broad mid-length scouting gradient at moderate temperature to elute all 10 compounds if possible and map the full retention window. This should reveal whether peaks are compressed early, late, or truncated so the next run can trim the phi window and adjust slope intelligently.

All compounds are resolved, so the priority is cutting t_last below 10 min while keeping the same selectivity. The observed elution window corresponds roughly to phi_e about 0.09 to 0.38, so a narrower, lower-organic gradient with shorter tG should keep all peaks inside the gradient and compress the run efficiently.

The run is still fully resolved, so push for a shorter last peak by slightly steepening the gradient and raising temperature. The weakest pair still has comfortable margin above 1.5, so there is room to trade some resolution for speed and try to get t_last under 10 min.

The near-coelution of peaks 6/7 at higher temperature shows this pair is temperature-sensitive, so revert to 40 C to restore selectivity while keeping the tighter phi window. A modestly longer gradient than run 3 should recover full resolution with only a small time penalty and may still beat the current best if t_last stays close to 10 min.

Run 2 had full resolution with comfortable margin, so the next step is to shorten tG while holding temperature at 40 C where the critical 6/7 pair remains separated. Keeping phi1 at 0.65 should help the late peak come off faster than with phi1 0.60 and may bring t_last near or below 10 min without sacrificing resolution.

You already have a perfect CRF, so explore a nearby variant that may preserve full resolution while adding a little extra push for the late peak and testing robustness around the optimum. Increasing phi1 slightly should mainly affect the tail of the gradient and hold region while leaving most early selectivity similar.

The optimum appears to sit near the resolution limit for pair 6/7, so test whether a slightly steeper gradient can still keep that pair at or above 1.5 while shortening the run further. This directly probes how much slope headroom remains around the current perfect method.

Pair 6/7 is the sole limiter and is sensitive to conditions, so test a lower temperature at the already optimal slope to see whether selectivity improves while keeping t_last under 10 min. A small retention increase is acceptable because injection 5 had 0.20 min margin on the time term.

A slightly narrower gradient window than the optimum may increase selectivity around the critical middle cluster while staying close enough in slope to preserve full resolution. This checks whether trimming high-organic space can improve the weakest pair without pushing t_last too far beyond 10 min.

Lowering phi0 slightly may spread the earliest and central peaks a bit differently without much impact on the late eluter, offering one more local selectivity probe around the perfect method. This tests whether the critical middle pair can be made more robust while still keeping the full run within the no-penalty time window.

Since lowering phi0 weakened the critical 6/7 pair, test the opposite direction with a slightly higher phi0 to see if the middle cluster gains selectivity while preserving the late peak under 10 min. This is a tight local probe around the proven optimum to map robustness of the starting composition.

Raising phi0 from 0.10 to 0.15 improved both t_last and the critical 6/7 resolution while keeping a perfect score, so continue in that direction to see whether the optimum is actually at a slightly higher starting composition. This probes whether the middle cluster can be compressed favorably without losing the first peak to the dead-time region.

The 0.15 start gave a perfect score and better margin on the critical pair than 0.10 or 0.20, so now test whether trimming phi1 from 0.65 to 0.60 can preserve full resolution while maintaining t_last under 10 min. This targets a potentially tighter, more focused gradient around the successful 0.15 start.

With phi0 = 0.15 giving the strongest margin on the critical pair, try a slightly higher phi1 to reduce late retention while checking whether 6/7 stays at or above 1.5. This is the most informative remaining local test around the two perfect methods.

The perfect methods at 40 C suggest the critical pair is close to the limit, but temperature also changes selectivity in a nontrivial way, so test whether a shallower gradient can offset the 45 C compression while benefiting from faster overall elution. This is a useful orthogonal probe to confirm whether temperature can ever outperform the 40 C optimum in combination with lower slope.

Having mapped the local optimum at 40 C, use one orthogonal corner case to separate slope and temperature effects on the critical region: lower temperature tends to alter pair identities while a steeper gradient compresses the run. This test will show whether the failure seen at 35 C was mainly temperature-driven or whether a shorter gradient shifts the critical overlap pattern in a useful way.

Complete the orthogonal map around the local optimum by testing the opposite temperature corner at the same short gradient. Comparing this directly with injection 16 will isolate whether temperature primarily swaps the critical overlap from 5/6 to 6/7 under steep conditions.

At 40 C, increasing phi1 from 0.65 to 0.70 shortened the run but hurt the 6/7 pair; one more step to 0.75 will define how sharply that tradeoff worsens and complete the local phi1 trend around the perfect methods. This helps bracket the robustness window while staying near the established optimum.

The optimum is already perfect, so use remaining runs to define the safe operating window; a longer gradient at the best 40 C and phi window should increase the 6/7 margin substantially. This provides a robustness anchor against the shorter, sharper methods that sit close to the resolution threshold.

The best region is clearly around 40 C with tG 10, and both higher phi0 and lower phi1 individually sharpened different aspects of the separation. Combining them tests whether the critical 6/7 pair can stay resolved while further shortening the late peak, giving one final local search point between the known perfect and near-perfect methods.

The 0.15/0.65/10 method is perfect at 40 C, and lowering temperature changed the critical overlap pattern at steeper slope; testing the same phi window at 35 C isolates pure temperature effect at the better starting composition. This final temperature check could reveal a second perfect region or confirm 40 C as uniquely optimal.

The 0.15 and 0.20 starts stayed near perfect, so one more increment in phi0 will define the upper edge of the robust start-composition window at the optimal slope and temperature. This tests whether the critical pair remains resolved or whether excessive early compression finally breaks the method.

With 40 C already mapped well, use one of the last runs to complete the low-temperature comparison at the same shorter gradient that exposed sensitivity at 0.15 start. This will confirm whether 35 C consistently shifts the critical failure to pair 5/6 regardless of phi0, improving confidence in the final mechanistic picture.

One last local probe can test whether combining the stronger 0.20 start with an even narrower upper window improves the critical 6/7 pair enough to offset a modest time increase. This explores the unexplored corner between 0.20/0.65 and 0.20/0.60, while staying at the clearly optimal temperature and slope family.

For the final run, probe one remaining 40 C corner that combines the strong 0.15 start with a narrower, steeper gradient to see whether the critical 6/7 pair can stay resolved while the late peak remains comfortably before 10 min. This is the last unexplored nearby condition around the perfect methods and may reveal whether a tighter focused window can still score 1.000.
